memoryVerse.text: And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.

source.details: Source ESV reads “And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good...” BSB 8:28a proposed as an excerpt: “And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him.” Verify with the teacher and https://ebible.org/engbsb/ROM08.htm before publication.

alsoVerifiedAt.details: Proposed excerpt from a public BSB text, teacher review needed.

sourceFiles.note: Original 12-page OT20 lesson, with seven Story Notes, teacher discussion questions, ten original review questions, memory verse, and extra activities. ESV source excerpt preserved in provenance; BSB proposed for worksheet display.

storyNotes.originalText: Jacob loved Joseph the most and gave him a beautiful robe. His brothers HATED him.
storyNotes.cleanText: Jacob loved Joseph the most and gave him a beautiful robe. His brothers hated him.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph had a dream where his brothers' bundles of GRAIN bowed down to his.
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph had a dream where his brothers' bundles of grain bowed down to his.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph dreamed of the sun, moon, and 11 STARS bowing to him. His brothers hated him more.
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph dreamed of the sun, moon, and 11 stars bowing to him. His brothers hated him more.

storyNotes.originalText: Jacob sent Joseph to check on his brothers. When they saw him coming, they said, “Let’s KILL him!”
storyNotes.cleanText: Jacob sent Joseph to check on his brothers. When they saw him coming, they said, “Let’s kill him!”

storyNotes.originalText: Reuben convinced them to throw Joseph into an empty PIT. He planned to rescue him later.
storyNotes.cleanText: Reuben convinced them to throw Joseph into an empty pit. He planned to rescue him later.

storyNotes.originalText: Instead of killing Joseph, they sold him as a SLAVE to traders headed for Egypt.
storyNotes.cleanText: Instead of killing Joseph, they sold him as a slave to traders headed for Egypt.

storyNotes.originalText: Using Joseph's robe, they fooled their father. He believed an ANIMAL ate Joseph.
storyNotes.cleanText: Using Joseph's robe, they fooled their father. He believed an animal ate Joseph.

questions.question: How many of you have a brother or a sister?

questions.question: How do you think Joseph's brothers felt about him being dad's favorite?

questions.question: How did Joseph's brothers feel after hearing yet another dream where they bowed down to their bratty brother?

questions.question: What did they do with Joseph’s robe?

finishStory.markedParagraph: Joseph was one of Jacob’s [twelve] sons. His father loved him very much and gave him a beautiful [robe]. Joseph’s brothers were [jealous] and would not speak kindly to him. God gave Joseph two [dreams]. In one dream, his brothers’ bundles of [grain] bowed to his bundle. In another, the sun, moon, and eleven [stars] bowed to him. Later, Jacob sent Joseph to check on his brothers. They took his robe and threw him in an empty [pit]. Reuben wanted to help him, but the brothers sold Joseph to [traders] going to [Egypt]. Then they stained his robe with [blood] and showed it to Jacob. Jacob thought a wild [animal] had killed Joseph. He was [sad] for a very long time.

reviewFlags.text: Original source uses an ESV excerpt of Romans 8:28a. Prepared worksheet verses propose the BSB excerpt “And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him.” Teacher must confirm translation, exact excerpt boundary, punctuation and rights.
Review six prepared Multiple Choice questions and twelve proposed incorrect answers.
Approve seven newly suggested false statements; inspect balance and clarity of the ten separately allocated Sort/True-False/Maze facts.
The source Big Idea displays lowercase “god” and joined words due to font/export layout. Prepared text normalizes it to “God”; original source remains unchanged.

The source describes Joseph’s brothers planning to kill him, throwing him into a pit, and selling him into slavery. Prepared activities use gentle wording where possible without changing the account; teacher should review for age group.
Inspect all six deliberate Circle the Mistakes errors and correction key for clarity and no accidental additional error.
Verify suggested wrong words in Odd Words and Checkboxes; separate word banks have no overlap.
Review four Small drawing prompts, six short Match the Words pairs, ten Crossword clues, and six Large Draw the Story captions.
Finish the Story has 678 characters including blanks, within the new 600–700 target; review whether the wording suits the age group.
Run the official repository validator, preflight, all relevant generators, and three numbered presets before publication. Ten different fact IDs are assigned but live print output is untested.
